days.heading: Piazza San Marco at kid pace

facts.label: Morning
facts.valueHtml: San Marco early, before the heat

facts.label: Optional
facts.valueHtml: Campanile lift for the lagoon view

days.note: Do the great square early while it is cool and half-empty. The free piazza and facade are the memory; the Campanile elevator is the one paid add-on worth it. Keep the afternoon loose.

spots.name: Piazza San Marco & St. Mark's Basilica
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · sanmarcoIG · veniceIG · basilicaFlickr

images.alt: St. Mark's Basilica facade and mosaics in Venice
Domes and spires of St. Mark's Basilica against the sky
Gondolas moored on the Venice lagoon at blue hour.

spots.cost: Piazza free. Basilica nave €10/person (pre-book). Campanile lift €15/person (~€60/family).
spots.climate: 82°F day / 68°F night — humid. The square bakes at midday; go early or at dusk.
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip the paid Basilica interior — the free piazza and facade are the photo. Saves €40–100 and keeps the day light, per the no-death-march plan.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Pre-book the Campanile lift (€60/family) for the 323-ft lagoon view — the elevator is far kinder on kid legs than the stairs.
spots.restoHtml:
• 1000 Gourmet Venezia — Neapolitan pizza near the piazza, reliably packed with families
  • Aciugheta — Venetian trattoria near San Zaccaria, wood-fired kids’ pizza plus cicchetti
  • 6342 A Le Tole — 30+ pizzas and housemade pasta in Castello
spots.altboxHtml:
• Doge’s Palace courtyard — free-adjacent and a better backup if the Basilica line feels like too much with kids.
  • Bridge of Sighs — a two-minute photo stop just behind the palace.
  • Gelato on the Riva — a waterfront cone with the lagoon view instead of a second church.

days.heading: Lago di Braies — the emerald warm-up

facts.label: Sleep
facts.valueHtml: San Vito di Cadore (Cortina) · night 2 of 5

days.note: Ease into the Dolomites with the gentlest, most famous lake. Go early — the valley closes to private cars at 9am from July 1 (reserve at prags.bz), and morning is when the water is a mirror.

spots.name: Lago di Braies
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · lagodibraiesIG · dolomitesIG · pragserwildseeFlickr

images.alt: Emerald Lago di Braies with its iconic boathouse and mountain wall
The Lago di Braies boathouse beneath steep Dolomite walls.
Emerald Lago di Braies reflecting the surrounding peaks.

spots.cost: Parking €7 (P2) to €12 (P3, lakeside). Rowboat: shared €20/person, private 45-min €55. Valley car-closed 9am–4pm from Jul 1 — reserve at prags.bz.
spots.climate: 60°F day / 42°F night at lake level (1,496m) — the cold lake keeps mornings crisp; go before 9am for glass-still reflections.
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip the boat and walk the free ~35-minute lakeshore loop — same emerald water, same boathouse, zero queue. Saves ~€55–80 for the family.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A private 45-minute rowboat (€55) at golden hour for the postcard frame — wooden hull, the boathouse behind you, the peaks doubled in the water.
spots.restoHtml:
• Panorama (Hotel Lago di Braies) — lake-view terrace, South Tyrolean; simple pasta for kids, reserve ahead
  • Chalet snack counter — fries, sandwiches, simple pasta, the fast picky-eater lunch
  • Ristorante Lago di Braies — independent lakeside spot, confirm pizza on the day’s menu
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lago di Carezza — a zero-hike, drive-up alpine lake below the Latemar with no reservation system.
  • Lago di Dobbiaco — a flat, stroller-easy lake loop close to the base.
  • Prato Piazza (Plätzwiese) — a high meadow plateau if the family wants views without a climb.

days.heading: Tre Cime di Lavaredo — the big one

facts.label: Sleep
facts.valueHtml: San Vito di Cadore (Cortina) · night 3 of 5

days.note: The signature Dolomites day. The toll road drives you to 2,333m so the loop starts high — the 8-year-old walks under the three peaks without a summit push, the 13-year-old gets a real trail. Start early to beat the storms — and from the same Rifugio Auronzo car park you can bolt on the short Cadini di Misurina viewpoint at sunrise (see below).

spots.name: Tre Cime di Lavaredo
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · trecimeIG · dreizinnenIG · dolomitesFlickr

images.alt: The Tre Cime massif viewed from the loop trail
Tre Cime's classic three-tower profile under high alpine light
Tre Cime rising beyond the calm surface of Lake Misurina.

spots.cost: Toll road to Rifugio Auronzo €40/car (pre-book a timed slot at auronzo.info). Rifugio lunch ~€60–80/family.
spots.climate: 62°F day / 38°F night at 2,333m — afternoon storms are common; start the loop by 9am and be down by mid-afternoon.
spots.saveHtml: Save Book the 7–9am toll slot for the best light and thinnest crowd, and pack sandwiches for the Locatelli viewpoint instead of a rifugio lunch (€15–18/plate × 4).
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Sleep at Rifugio Locatelli (~€60–70/person half-board) to get the blue-hour and sunrise faces without the day-trippers — bring cash, the huts don’t take cards.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rifugio Auronzo — self-service at the trailhead: pasta, wurstel, fries, polenta; easiest kid meal on the mountain
  • Rifugio Locatelli — the classic Three-Peaks view hut; plain polenta for picky eaters
  • Rifugio Lavaredo — trailside on the loop, same Alpine self-service and a good fallback if Locatelli is packed
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lago di Sorapis — a harder, quieter hike to a milky-turquoise lake (fixed cables) for the 13-year-old.
  • Monte Piana — a WWI open-air museum plateau above Lago di Misurina with trenches, tunnels, and 360° views.
  • Lago di Misurina lakeshore — the easy, flat option at the foot of the toll road if legs are done.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Tre Cime Loop Trail GuideThe Ultimate Tre Cime Guide (2026)

spots.name: Cadini di Misurina Viewpoint
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · cadinidimisurinaIG · dolomitesIG · misurinaFlickr

images.alt: Sunlit Cadini limestone spires rising above the trail
The Cadini promontory and its serrated limestone needles
Sunrise color washing the Cadini peaks.

spots.cost: No extra toll — same Rifugio Auronzo car park as Tre Cime (€40/car, one timed slot covers both). The viewpoint hike itself is free: ~3.9km out-and-back, ~1hr, only 144m of gain on path #117.
spots.climate: Easy hike, one exposed catch. Short and mostly gentle from the car park — but the famous photo promontory is a narrow ridge with cliff drop-offs. Doable with kids if you keep the 8-year-old close and stop short of the knife-edge tip; the 13-year-old is fine with care in dry weather. A right-side contour path skips the exposed crest entirely. Skip it if wet, icy, or windy.
spots.saveHtml: Save This is the rare free epic — no lift, no separate ticket. Do it first, at sunrise, before the Tre Cime loop while the light rakes the needles and the ridge is empty, then walk back to the car and start the big loop.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a local sunrise photo guide from Misurina — they know exactly where the family can stand safely for the postcard frame and handle the pre-dawn timing so you don't.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rifugio Auronzo — right at the trailhead; self-service pasta, wurstel, fries before or after the walk
  • Rifugio Col de Varda — the hut path #117 heads toward; chairlift-served, easy add for a strudel stop
  • Lakeside at Lago di Misurina — pizza and gelato by the lake at the foot of the toll road
spots.altboxHtml:
• Right-side contour path — the same viewpoint area without going over the exposed crest, if heights are a concern.
  • Lago di Misurina loop — a flat, stroller-easy lakeshore walk with a playground if the family skips the ridge.
  • Monte Piana — a WWI trench-and-tunnel plateau above the lake for a history-flavored alternative.

days.heading: Seceda’s ridge by cable car

facts.label: Sleep
facts.valueHtml: San Vito di Cadore (Cortina) · night 4 of 5

facts.label: Walk
facts.valueHtml: Ridge stroll, or hike down via Rifugio Firenze

days.note: The cable car does the climbing so everyone stands on the 2,500m Seceda ridge — the tilted-earth view of the Odle spires. Do the ridge walk before noon; willing hikers can ride up one-way and walk down to turn the ticket into the day’s trek.

spots.name: Seceda & Alpe di Siusi
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · secedaIG · alpedisiusiIG · valgardenaFlickr

images.alt: Seceda's knife-edge ridge and Odle spires
Seceda’s serrated ridge under sweeping alpine sky.
A dramatic Seceda panorama with cloud-wrapped spires.

spots.cost: Ortisei–Seceda cableway round trip ~€74 adult / €37 junior (8–15), under-8 free — ~€222/family. Timed-slot pre-booking required.
spots.climate: 57°F day / 38°F night on the 2,500m ridge — very exposed and windy; do the ridge walk before noon, before the storms build.
spots.saveHtml: Save Buy one-way UP (€49 adult/€25 junior) and hike down via Rifugio Firenze — it turns the priciest ticket of the leg into the day’s epic hike and saves ~€25/adult.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The full Seceda–Rifugio Firenze–Baita Troier circuit with a mid-ridge rifugio lunch — a half-day alpine trek under the Odle spires with three hut stops.
spots.restoHtml:
• Baita Sanon — Alpe di Siusi, family-run Tyrolean/Ladin, explicitly kid-friendly, plain plates on request
  • Rifugio Firenze — on the ridge circuit; pasta, polenta, dumplings and an Odle-peaks terrace
  • Ristorante Bullaccia (Puflatsch) — Alpe di Siusi, fast-serving South Tyrolean for small kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Passo Giau — drive up the switchbacks to a wide-open meadow saddle with 360° views; no cable car, no timed slot.
  • Alpe di Siusi (Compatsch) — Europe’s largest alpine meadow, gentle and stroller-friendly by its own gondola.
  • Ortisei town — a pretty Val Gardena stroll if the ridge is socked in.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Best Way to Visit SecedaSeceda–Rifugio Firenze Circuit

days.heading: Cinque Torri & Cortina — the lighter day

facts.label: Sleep
facts.valueHtml: San Vito di Cadore (Cortina) · night 5 of 5

days.note: Use the short Cinque Torri loop for a lighter alpine finale: WWI trenches beneath wild towers, then Cortina for a stroll and gelato.

spots.name: Cinque Torri
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · cinquetorriIG · dolomitesIG · cortinaFlickr

images.alt: Cinque Torri rising over an alpine meadow
Cinque Torri standing above the high alpine meadow.
Cinque Torri rising from a wide alpine plateau.

spots.cost: Chairlift return €27.50 adult (one-way €20.50); under-8 free, minors discounted — budget ~€75–85/family. 5% card discount in 2026.
spots.climate: 60°F day / 40°F night at Rifugio Scoiattoli (2,225m) — short and easy, so it forgives a late-morning start after a slow breakfast.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pay by credit card at the base for the built-in 5% discount, then walk the free ~2km WWI-trench loop once you’re up — one of the cheapest “epic scenery” stops of the whole trip.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Add the beginner via-ferrata-lite from Rifugio Scoiattoli toward Averau (short, guided) for the 13-year-old — a real climbing memory while the rest of the family relaxes on the terrace.
spots.restoHtml:
• Rifugio Scoiattoli — right under the towers; casunziei ravioli and polenta, flag ahead for a plain-pasta kid plate
  • Rifugio Averau — a 30-min walk on, sommelier-run homemade pasta; confirm a simple option
  • Rifugio Cinque Torri — casual at the base of the towers; casunziei, ricotta strudel, homemade bread
spots.altboxHtml:
• Rifugio Lagazuoi — a 5-minute cable car to a WWI tunnel network and a panoramic hut at Passo Falzarego.
  • Nuvolau / Averau loop — a longer scramble to a 360° summit view for the strong-legged.
  • Lago Ghedina — a quiet, forest-ringed little lake near Cortina for an easy afternoon.
spots.bloglinksHtml: Cinque Torri Hike & RifugiosCinque Torri with Kids

spots.name: Cortina d'Ampezzo & the Faloria Cable Car
spots.exploreHtml: PhotosIG · cortinaIG · dolomitesIG · faloriaFlickr

images.alt: Aerial view of Cinque Torri and the Tofana wall above Cortina
The Tofane wall dominating the Cortina skyline.
A high Dolomite pass above the Cortina region.

spots.cost: Faloria cable car ~€27 adult / ~€20 under-16 (~€94/family). Freccia nel Cielo to Cima Tofana €45 adult round trip.
spots.climate: 65°F day / 45°F night in town (1,224m) — mornings are the reliably clear window; storms roll through most afternoons.
spots.saveHtml: Save Ride Faloria (~half the price of Freccia nel Cielo) for a comparable panorama, and window-shop Corso Italia for free — the 2026-Olympics town is a stroll, not a ticket.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Freccia nel Cielo all the way to Cima Tofana (3,244m, €45 adult) — the single highest, most dramatic viewpoint reachable without technical climbing on the whole trip.
spots.restoHtml:
• Ristorante Pizzeria 5 Torri — Corso Italia, busy family standby, traditional pizza and pasta
  • Pizzeria Ai Due Forni — town center, pizza by the slice or whole, the fast post-hike dinner
  • El Camineto — above town with a valley view; polenta, grilled meats, simple pasta for kids
spots.altboxHtml:
• Lago di Sorapis viewpoint (Passo Tre Croci) — roadside massif views instead of a second cable car if legs are tired.
  • Rifugio Lagazuoi + WWI tunnels — a cable-car-and-history half day at Passo Falzarego.
  • Mercato / gelato on Corso Italia — a low-key town afternoon before the flight south.
